text:
sophie_support: Hey team, merchant 'Brightly' reporting ~12% spike in card declines over the last 2 hours. Most failures report AVS/CVV mismatch even though customer says card + address were correct. Example txn IDs: txn_8f7a1c, txn_8f7b2d, txn_8f7c3e

sophie_support: Pasted one raw request/response from our gateway: 
```http
POST /v1/payments HTTP/1.1
Host: gateway.redwood.example
{
  "amount": 1299,
  "currency": "USD",
  "card": {
    "number": "**** **** **** 4242",
    "exp_month": 12,
    "exp_year": 2027,
    "cvc": "***"
  },
  "billing_address": {
    "line1": "123 São Jorge St, Apt. #5B",
    "city": "San José",
    "postal_code": "95112",
    "country": "US"
  }
}

Response:
{
  "status": "declined",
  "avs_result": "N",
  "cvv_result": "N",
  "gateway_code": "05",
  "acquirer_message": "Do not honor"
}
```

sophie_support: Merchant insists same card worked minutes earlier for other txns. They attached a customer screenshot showing address exactly as above.

omar_payments: Thanks, pulling logs. Quick q — are declines concentrated by card BIN or acquirer?

jess_ops: From our dash: 9/12 failures hit Acquirer-A (acquirer_id: acq_01), 3 hit Acquirer-B. BIN distribution broad.

omar_payments: Can you paste raw gateway request we sent to Acquirer-A for one of those txns? need to see address normalization fields.

liam_research: I grabbed one: 
```
acq_request: {
  "amount":1299,
  "billing_line1":"123 So Jorge St Apt #5B",
  "billing_city":"San Jose",
  "billing_postal":"95112",
  "country":"US"
}

acq_response: {
  "status":"declined",
  "avs":"N",
  "cvv":"N",
  "acq_code":"05",
  "acq_text":"DECLINED - AVS MISMATCH"
}
```

liam_research: Notice our pipeline injected NUL bytes when removing unicode normalization (bug from a sanitizer lib). That could mangle the address on the wire.

omar_payments: Oof. NULs would definitely break AVS matching at most issuers — they do exact string compares. Good catch.

jess_ops: Is this only for customers with diacritics (São, José) or any unicode punctuation?

liam_research: Looks like any non-ASCII characters we try to strip using the sanitizer produce "\u0000" placeholders. Before the sanitizer patch this month we sent the unicode as-is; Acquirer-A used to accept it. After the sanitizer, many addresses end up with NULs.

acquirer-contact: From the bank side — AVS runs against the address on file. Non-printable chars or embedded NUL will fail pattern matching and often return AVS = N. CVV = N likely from separate check failing due to general decline code if AVS fails risk policy. We see "Do not honor" when issuer blocks on mismatch.

omar_payments: Immediate mitigation: 1) Roll back sanitizer change on the payments path (canary) OR 2) sanitize by replacing diacritics with ASCII equivalents (normalize NFKD then remove combining marks) and ensure no NUL bytes. Which is faster?

liam_research: Rolling back the sanitizer on payments path is fastest — I can push a canary within 10 minutes. I'll also prepare a small lib to do proper unicode normalization and strip combining marks.

jess_ops: Merchant wants guidance for customers in the meantime. Suggest message: "If you have accented characters in your billing address try re-entering without accents or use numeric apartment field (e.g., Apt 5B)" — but we should avoid customer-facing technical noise.

sophie_support: I'll send Brightly a short note: we're investigating, quick workaround: re-enter address with ASCII characters or remove punctuation. Also ask them to retry the declined txns to see if they go through.

payments-bot: deploy.canary triggered by liam_research at 1797602800 — rollout to payments-canary-01

payments-bot: canary health: PASS (10/10) - no downstream errors for 5m

omar_payments: After canary we should re-run 20 recent failed txns in sandbox mode (resubmit with same tokens) to verify AVS result flips to Y/A. Who can run repro?

liam_research: I'll replay 20 samples to Acquirer-A via the canary endpoint. Will post results in 15m.

(15 minutes later)

liam_research: Replay results: 20/20 now show avs_result: Y (address match), cvv_result: M (match/indeterminate) for two cards, and approvals on 18/20; 2 still declined with code 05 (issuer-side hard decline unrelated to AVS).

omar_payments: Great — confirms sanitizer change was root cause. Next steps: 1) Roll canary to prod for payments ingestion only after safety window, 2) hotfix sanitizer lib to use unicode normalization instead of NUL insertion, 3) notify merchants impacted and provide workaround, 4) open incident/SEV for audit and RCA.

jess_ops: I'll draft the merchant notice and coordinate refunds/retries where needed.

sophie_support: Merchant notified, they acknowledged and will retry. They asked for a list of affected txn IDs to reconcile. I'll share the 12 IDs we saw.

omAR_payments: (typo) sorry — omar_payments: Filing SEV-719 for RCA and timeline. Assigning to eng-payments and eng-ml for sanitizer audit.

liam_research: I'll create PR for normalization lib and include unit tests for accented names/addresses and ensure no NUL bytes in output.

acquirer-contact: We'll mark the three persistent failures as issuer declined and add that to the ticket. No further action needed from acquirer while issuer investigates.

sophie_support: Thanks everyone :tada: — closing loop with merchant after retries. I'll update SEV-719 with merchant confirmation.

jess_ops: Nice catch, Liam. Good triage flow. :thumbsup:

payments-bot: SEV-719 created and linked to incident channel #incidents-719
